writhe0_lemma.statement: For any normalised Markov trace on H_3(q) (sum_lambda y_lambda d_lambda = 1, d = (1,2,1)) and any braid beta in B_3 with writhe 0 and pi(beta) = id: tr_M(beta) = 1 + y_(2,1) * (chi^(2,1)(beta) - 2).
writhe0_lemma.consequence_true: the SPLIT between y_(3) and y_(1^3) is invisible on such braids (only their normalisation-pinned sum enters).
writhe0_lemma.consequence_false: y_(2,1) is NOT invisible. Two conventions agree on such a braid iff they share y_(2,1) or chi^(2,1)(beta) = 2.

negative_stabilisation.definition: z_minus := z - h, h = q - q^-1; forced by sigma_n^-1 = sigma_n - h in axiom 3 (rem:markov-axioms-primitive). The FORMULA is convention-independent -- it holds for every member of the Ocneanu family; only its value moves.
negative_stabilisation.bar_involution: Under q -> q^-1: z_C is bar-INVARIANT (z_C = q^(1/2)/(q+1) = bar z_C), whereas z_D is NOT: bar z_D = 1/(q^3+q). Note the identity bar z_D = z_minus_D exactly -- under convention D the positive and negative stabilisation parameters are bar-conjugate. Verified symbolically 2026-08-08 (sympy, exact cancellation).
negative_stabilisation.bar_invariance_caveat: content/quantum-observable-universe/braids-and-knots/bar-involution-c5-algebraic-identities.md asserts 'the Markov parameter z is bar-invariant'. That is TRUE for C and FALSE for D, so it is one of the corpus statements that a future z change to D would falsify. Its companion factorisation h = (q^(1/2)-q^(-1/2))(q^(1/2)+q^(-1/2)) is an identity in q alone and is unaffected; only the naming of q^(1/2)+q^(-1/2) as 1/z is convention-bound.
negative_stabilisation.z_independent_consequences: The root pair of z*z_minus = 1, namely z = q and z = -q^-1 (the two one-dimensional characters, both degenerate), depends only on h and is therefore identical under every convention. So is the z^k factor for appending k stabilised strands. Verified 2026-08-08.

open_item.blast_radius: ~30 F_Bor consumers; -197 ppm on m_p. Closing it the OTHER way -- moving the DEFINITIONAL side from C to D by rewriting z in the braids-and-knots blocks -- is not cheap either: as of 2026-08-08 at least 8 corpus sites stipulate or derive from z = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), including thm:jones-markov-trace itself (the block rem:markov-axioms-primitive cites), jones-markov-trace.lean, prf:trm-hopf-sigma1-sq-closed-form, prf:trace-locality-meets-gs-nonlocality, prf:hecke-satisfies-blitvic-hypothesis, rem:bar-involution-c5-algebraic-identities (whose bar-invariance claim holds for C and FAILS for D), prop:centered-hecke-variance-positive (+ its proof, which uses (q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})^2 > 4), and prf:algebraic-gns-embedding. It would also flip the `binding` channel from agreed to disputed, since binding's definitional_source is that same line while binding production is C. Inventory: docs/audits/2026-08-08-markov-axioms-naming-vs-z-value.md.
open_item.note: OWNER DECISION. No agent may switch the production trace to close this, and no agent may close it from the definitional side either -- rewriting z from C to D in the braids-and-knots definition blocks decides the same question in the same forbidden way, just from the other end. D is the value that lands on CODATA, which is exactly why deciding by match is forbidden here. What WAS done on 2026-08-08 (and is not a decision): the naming defect in rem:markov-axioms-primitive and the false Jones-polynomial sentence in thm:jones-markov-trace were corrected, so both blocks now say plainly which family member their stipulated z is. The dispute is unchanged and stays open.

It traces atom_braid_word_3A (computations/mass_at_3A_proper.py:256), which for (Z,N)=(1,0) is an 11-crossing word whose core is sigma_0^3 sigma_1^-3 -- a different braid closure from the 6-crossing interleaved beta_Bor = (sigma_0 sigma_1^-1)^3.
